tools.name: onyx_decide
tools.description: Return allow / review / deny for a counterparty address against your own risk policy, with the reasons named. Use this before every outbound transfer. Checks issuer blacklists (USDT, USDC), sanctions across six EVM chains plus the OFAC list, open scam databases, community reports and behavioural patterns. Costs credit.

address.description: Blockchain address (TRON, Ethereum or other EVM, Solana)

amount_usd.description: Amount you intend to send, in USD. Used only if your policy caps amounts.

policy.description: Optional. Omit for a conservative default that returns review for anything unknown.

tools.name: onyx_screen
tools.description: Return the raw risk markers for one address: risk zone, issuer blacklists, sanctions coverage, scam databases, community reports, address age, balance and exchange attribution where known. Use this when you want the facts rather than a decision. Costs credit.

address.description: Blockchain address (TRON, Ethereum or other EVM, Solana)

tools.name: onyx_screen_batch
tools.description: Screen up to 50 addresses in a single call, for example before a mass payout. Priced per address, and only addresses actually screened are charged. Each result carries facts_complete so you can tell whether the behavioural facts finished loading.

items.description: Blockchain address (TRON, Ethereum or other EVM, Solana)

tools.name: onyx_preflight
tools.description: Operational safety check for a payment, separate from risk screening. Detects address poisoning (a lookalike planted in your history so it gets copied instead of the real address), burn addresses, token contracts and other contract recipients that would swallow the tokens (a Safe multisig or an EIP-7702 delegated wallet is reported as a wallet, not a trap), and addresses that behave differently on different chains. Pass known_addresses (the counterparties you already use) to enable poisoning detection. Verdicts: stop, caution, clear, or unknown: on EVM chains the recipient check could not run (retry, not charged); on TRON and Solana only the lookalike check exists (partial: true) and known_addresses is required. In our live-traffic sample this class of loss came up far more often than sanctioned counterparties. Dedicated transaction-security services cover part of it; no AML screening does. Run this together with onyx_decide before every payment.

address.description: Blockchain address (TRON, Ethereum or other EVM, Solana)

items.description: Blockchain address (TRON, Ethereum or other EVM, Solana)

known_addresses.description: Addresses you have used before, so a lookalike can be spotted. Strongly recommended.

chain.description: The chain you are about to pay on. The recipient is then judged on that chain (a Safe or a contract exists only where it was deployed). Without it Ethereum and Base are read.

tools.name: onyx_trace
tools.description: Multi-hop trace of outgoing flows from an address, with attribution where a node is known (exchange labels, deposit addresses). Use it to establish provenance after receiving funds. Costs more than a screening call.

address.description: Blockchain address (TRON, Ethereum or other EVM, Solana)

tools.name: onyx_watch
tools.description: Subscribe to an address. When it enters an issuer blacklist, a sanctions list or a scam database, we POST a signed event to your callback URL. A one-off check cannot warn you about a freeze that has not happened yet. Billed per address per day. The callback must be public https.

address.description: Blockchain address (TRON, Ethereum or other EVM, Solana)

callback_url.description: Public https URL to receive events

tools.name: onyx_balance
tools.description: How much credit your API key has left, and the current prices. Free.

tools.name: onyx_payment_info
tools.description: Machine-readable payment terms: which asset and network to send, the address, prices per operation, and how to claim an API key from the address you paid from. No account or signup is involved. Free, and works without a key.
